## The problem

Gene lists arrive from papers, spreadsheets and colleagues with whatever
symbols their authors used: aliases (`HER2`), old symbols (`SEPT1`), symbols
HGNC has withdrawn, and names that are simply not symbols at all. Before such
a list can be joined to DrugBank targets, HPO phenotypes or anything else, each
entry has to be mapped to an approved HGNC symbol, and the ambiguous ones have
to be seen, not guessed.

This article does that with `parseHGNC()` and `dplyr` on the HGNC sample that
ships with `dbparser`. It runs offline in a few seconds.

```{r setup}
library(dbparser)
library(dplyr)
```

## The list

```{r}
genes <- c("PD1", "PDL1", "HER2", "SEPT1", "MARCH1", "FOX1",
           "CBBM", "A12M1", "TP53")
```

The bundled sample holds only 24 genes and a few withdrawn entries, so every
input above was chosen to be in it (or, for `FOX1`, to show what a miss looks
like). On HGNC's full files the same code covers all approved genes; see
[Full data](#full-data) below.

## Parse the HGNC sample

```{r}
hgnc_dir <- system.file("extdata", "hgnc", package = "dbparser")
hgnc <- parseHGNC(file.path(hgnc_dir, "hgnc_complete_set.txt"),
                  withdrawn_path = file.path(hgnc_dir, "withdrawn.txt"))

names(hgnc)
nrow(hgnc$gene)
```

Every `dvobject` records where its data came from, including the licence and
the citation HGNC asks for:

```{r}
glimpse(get_source_metadata(hgnc))
```

HGNC publishes no release number for its current files, so `release`,
`release_date` and `retrieved_at` are `NA` here; pass them to `parseHGNC()`
when you parse your own download.

## Match each input

`gene_name` has one row per approved symbol, alias and previous symbol (and
the names, which we do not need here). Each row carries its gene's
`hgnc_id`, so a match gives the approved symbol directly.

```{r}
approved <- hgnc$gene |>
  select(hgnc_id, matched = symbol)

name_hits <- hgnc$gene_name |>
  filter(kind %in% c("symbol", "alias_symbol", "prev_symbol")) |>
  inner_join(approved, by = "hgnc_id") |>
  transmute(input = name,
            matched,
            how = recode(kind,
                         symbol       = "approved",
                         alias_symbol = "alias",
                         prev_symbol  = "previous"))
```

Withdrawn symbols are in their own table, with the gene or genes HGNC merged
or split them into. An entry withdrawn outright points nowhere.

```{r}
withdrawn_hits <- hgnc$withdrawn |>
  transmute(input   = withdrawn_symbol,
            matched = merged_into_symbol,
            how     = "withdrawn")
```

Join the list to both, keeping every match: an input that fits several genes
gets several rows here.

```{r}
hits <- tibble(input = genes) |>
  left_join(bind_rows(name_hits, withdrawn_hits),
            by = "input", relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  distinct()

hits
```

## One row per input

Collapse to one row per input. `needs_choice` is `TRUE` when an input fits
more than one approved gene; these are listed, not resolved.

```{r}
clean <- hits |>
  group_by(input) |>
  summarise(
    needs_choice = n_distinct(na.omit(matched)) > 1,
    how          = if (all(is.na(how))) "no match"
                   else paste(unique(na.omit(how)), collapse = ", "),
    matched      = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(matched))), collapse = ", "),
    .groups      = "drop") |>
  select(input, matched, how, needs_choice) |>
  arrange(match(input, genes))

knitr::kable(clean)
```

What the table shows:

- **`TP53`** is an approved symbol; nothing to do.
- **`HER2`** and **`PDL1`** are aliases of `ERBB2` and `CD274`.
- **`SEPT1`** and **`MARCH1`** are previous symbols: HGNC renamed them
  `SEPTIN1` and `MARCHF1`. The `gene` table has the date of each change.
- **`PD1`** is an alias of three genes (`PDCD1`, `SNCA` and `SPATA2`). Most
  readers mean `PDCD1`, but the list does not say so, and only its author can.
- **`CBBM`** is a previous symbol of both `OPN1LW` and `OPN1MW`, and HGNC's
  withdrawn file records it as split into the same two genes, so it needs a
  choice too.
- **`A12M1`** was withdrawn and points to no gene.
- **`FOX1`** finds nothing. In this sample `RBFOX1` has the alias `FOX-1`,
  with a hyphen; exact matching does not guess that the two are the same.

```{r}
hgnc$gene |>
  filter(symbol %in% c("SEPTIN1", "MARCHF1")) |>
  select(symbol, prev_symbol, date_symbol_changed)
```

## Withdrawn symbols

The withdrawn table keeps HGNC's own status for the withdrawn ID and for each
gene it points to:

```{r}
hgnc$withdrawn |>
  filter(withdrawn_symbol %in% genes) |>
  select(withdrawn_symbol, status, merged_into_symbol, merged_into_status)
```

## Next steps

Inputs with `needs_choice = TRUE`, a `withdrawn` match with no target, or no
match at all go back to whoever wrote the list. The rest map one-to-one to an
approved symbol and can be joined to other sources, for example DrugBank
targets or HPO gene-phenotype associations.

## Full data {#full-data}

The sample is enough to show the method, not to clean a real list. The script
[`announce/hgnc_full.R`](https://github.com/ropensci/dbparser/blob/cran/announce/hgnc_full.R)
in the package repository runs the same steps on your own download of
`hgnc_complete_set.txt` and `withdrawn.txt` from
[genenames.org](https://www.genenames.org/download/statistics-and-files/).
